ai.title: SDK: Simplify text chunk handling in run.ts
ai.summary: Removed per-agent text filtering state and event caching logic in sdk/src/run.ts. Text chunks are now handled directly without intermediate state tracking or pending flushes. This simplifies the streaming pipeline and reduces memory overhead by eliminating redundant Map structures.

eli5.text: You may have noticed the assistant's text output sometimes included leftover tool-related markup or stuttered when an agent handed work to a sub-agent. Behind the scenes, the code that stitched together each incoming snippet of the assistant's reply was keeping several separate lists of text per agent, filtering out XML-like fragments piece by piece and re-emitting trimmed copies through an extra cache layer. That bookkeeping has been removed: snippets now flow through a single path and are emitted as they arrive, so there is less redundant state to keep in sync and the output you see is assembled directly from the chunks the assistant produces. The feature set is unchanged; this is purely a streamlining of how the streaming text is handled, and it is live today.

ai.title: Revert subagent chunk forwarding and stream parser changes
ai.summary: Reverts npm-app and agent-runtime changes from de8997f72f1. Removes onlyChildAgents and emitPromptChunkToParser logic from Client, eliminating subagent chunk forwarding to the XML parser. Updates stream-parser.ts to access chunk.text directly instead of passing the full chunk object.

eli5.text: If you were watching an assistant that spins off helper subagents, those helpers used to stream their word-by-word responses back through a shared text interpreter, which let the main assistant see and react to their live output. That forwarding path has now been removed, so subagent responses are still stored and displayed, but they no longer route through the shared live-text system. The change landed on 2025-10-23 and affects the assistant runtime and client; if you watched subagent streaming closely you might notice fewer live updates from helpers, since their output goes to storage and screen refresh only rather than also piping into the parser. Because it is described as a revert, the behavior is effectively the original behavior before the subagent streaming wiring was added.

ai.summary: scripts/dev.sh now runs bun --cwd=sdk run build after server readiness. SDK build failure terminates server and exits. Ensures client starts with updated SDK.

eli5.text: When developers start the local development server for building and testing the assistant, the system now automatically builds the assistant's core toolkit first to make sure it's up to date. If that toolkit build fails, the server stops immediately instead of trying to launch with an outdated version. You wouldn't notice this as an end user, but developers running local tests will get a clearer failure if the toolkit doesn't compile properly.

eli5.text: When you use the command-line version of the tool and it's working or waiting on something, the status message and the toggle that switches the assistant between manual and automatic modes now sit side by side on the same line instead of staggering vertically. The status bar stays centered while the toggle lines up neatly next to it, so the bottom row of the interface looks aligned rather than having the toggle dropped lower than the status text. This only affects the terminal interface layout and is live today for anyone running the command-line tool.

ai.title: cleanup-worktree.sh supports bulk removal
ai.summary: scripts/cleanup-worktree.sh now accepts optional argument for single or bulk worktree cleanup. Refactored into `cleanup_worktree` function handling git worktree removal, `.env.worktree` deletion, and directory cleanup. Defaults to removing all worktrees in `../codebuff-worktrees` when no argument provided. Changed from `set -e` to `set +e` to continue cleanup on errors.

eli5.text: When you run the cleanup tool without specifying a particular worktree, it now clears out all leftover worktrees at once instead of requiring you to name each one individually. The script has also gotten more resilient: if one worktree fails to clean up (for example, because it has uncommitted changes), it will force-remove it or simply move on and continue with the rest rather than stopping entirely. This means a single stuck or dirty worktree won't prevent the other worktrees from being cleaned up.

ai.title: Update tool-handlers.test.ts
ai.summary: Test assertion in `tool-handlers.test.ts` now uses `toHaveProperty` instead of `toContainKey`. This aligns with standard Jest matchers for checking object properties.

eli5.text: A small behind-the-scenes tweak was made to one of the project's internal test files, which developers use to make sure new changes behave as expected; this swap doesn't affect anything you see or use. The team updated the way a check is written in that test file, but the feature itself and how the tool behaves remain unchanged.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.504
ai.summary: This release bundles fourteen days of same-day work across the Freebuff monorepo into a single version increment. The package version in npm-app/release/package.json advances from 1.0.503 to 1.0.504, aggregating features such as the CLI agent mode toggle (base2-fast/base2-max), Ghostty dark-mode detection, local .agents directory loading, hidden context-pruner subagent output, and the SDK promptAiSdkStream/structured LLM path now wired into the agent runtime. Additional notable changes include the removal of processStream from the SDK surface, runId propagation through agent runtime and SDK contracts, and staging deploy CI refactored around Bun with a [codecane] trigger prefix. Internal agent refactors expanded base2 variants, added Buffy the Orchestrator and file-researcher agents, and moved callMainPrompt into the agent-runtime package.
ai.evidence: Commit 913a3c0e modifies only npm-app/release/package.json, changing the version field from 1.0.503 to 1.0.504. No other source files are touched, confirming this is a pure release bump. The same-day sequence shows 15 prior commits spanning CLI layout, SDK streaming, agent runtime, eval config, and prompt refactors that are all captured under this release.

eli5.text: You can now choose between two AI power modes right from your terminal, letting you pick either a fast-responding assistant (base2-fast) or a deeper-thinking one (base2-max) with a simple Shift+Tab toggle or mouse click. The terminal interface learned to hide internal helper chatter so only the work that matters shows up on screen, making your coding sessions cleaner and less distracting. Local project-specific AI agents can now be dropped into a.agents folder and automatically loaded, so teams can share custom AI behaviors without touching your main installation. Streaming output from the AI now handles text chunks more efficiently, using less memory while keeping conversations smooth, and the tool that lets programs talk to multiple AI providers at once got smarter about routing requests to OpenAI, Anthropic, and others. Dark mode is now the default for Ghostty terminal users, and you can type natural-language questions directly to an AI helper using the new /ask command in your terminal.

ai.title: Fix base2 agent ID and stepPrompt logic
ai.summary: Corrected `id` to `base2-gpt-5-worker-simple` in `.agents/base2/base2-gpt-5-worker-simple.ts` to match filename. Updated `stepPrompt` in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` to conditionally inject `generate-plan` for normal mode or `base2-gpt-5-worker` for max mode, replacing previous boolean logic. Scope limited to internal agent configuration files. Change ensures proper agent spawning based on execution mode.

eli5.text: The internal assistant that helps build software inside the company now correctly identifies itself when it starts up, so it doesn't get confused about which version it is. When someone runs it in normal mode (the default), it will add a planning step before doing work, but in max mode (the more powerful version), it skips that planning step and goes straight to doing the work itself. This only affects people using these internal development assistants today.

ai.summary: Added new agent definitions for `base2-fast-subgoals`, `base2-gpt-5-worker-simple`, and `base2-max-simple` under `.agents/base2/`. Updated `base2-gpt-5-worker` to use `createBase2('max')` instead of `createBase2('normal')`. Modified `evals/buffbench/main.ts` to run only `base2-max` and `base2-max-simple` with `taskConcurrency` increased to 10.

eli5.text: If you run the BuffBench evaluation, it now only tests two specific assistant configurations (the strongest one and its simplified version) instead of four, and it runs them twice as fast by handling more tasks at the same time. At the same time, the team added two new pre-built assistant types and gave the existing GPT-5 worker a more powerful engine, so it can tackle harder tasks. These changes are live today for anyone running these internal evaluations.

eli5.text: Searching for code using the built-in search tool has started working again after a recent fix. The change restores how the search tool finds and runs its search engine: in developer mode it uses a pre-installed search engine, and in the release version the app unpacks a hidden copy of it the first time you need it, keeping a backup ready if anything goes wrong. You would notice this if you tried to search your codebase and it now returns results instead of failing, with the underlying recovery steps handled automatically behind the scenes.

eli5.text: The instructions given to the internal coding assistant were tightened up to keep its changes smaller and more careful, to look up existing code before refactoring, and to run its own unit tests before considering a task done. A new section was also added to the assistant's prompt template. This only affects how the assistant behaves internally and has no impact on the software you see today.

eli5.text: The assistant has been taught a new rule: once it announces it has finished a task, it must fall silent and not say anything else. Engineers also added several experimental assistant modes for an upcoming internal evaluation, so test runs can compare how different thinking approaches behave. These new modes only affect the test environment today and are not turned on for regular use.

ai.title: base2 drops normal mode and validator agents
ai.summary: base2 agents now use 'fast' mode exclusively, removing 'normal' and 'max' variants. Deleted files include base2-gpt-5-planner, base2-hybrid-max, and base2-max-simple. The base2-gpt-5-worker no longer spawns code-reviewer-gpt-5 or validator-gpt-5, simplifying orchestration to file-picker and code-searcher only. Eval harness in evals/buffbench/main.ts updated to reflect these agent definition changes.

eli5.text: The coding assistant no longer checks its own work or runs validation steps before finishing, it skips those review and testing phases entirely. If you watched it work, you'd see it make edits and then immediately wrap up, without spinning up extra helper agents to double-check the results. This makes each coding task finish faster, but removes the built-in quality checks that used to happen between writing and completing the changes.

ai.title: Reorganize base2 agent definitions into subdirectories
ai.summary: Moved base2 agent variants into specific subdirectories (alloy, task-researcher, orchestrator) and deleted unused files like base2-with-task-researcher-full.ts. Updated import paths in .agents/base2/base2-gpt-5.ts and related files to reflect the new structure. This internal refactor cleans up the agent definition hierarchy without changing runtime behavior.

eli5.text: The team reorganized how the base2 assistant variants are stored on the internal server, moving them into clearly labeled folders (alloy, task-researcher, orchestrator) and deleting an old unused variant. Nothing you see changes today because the runtime behavior stayed the same, but the housekeeping means future edits to specific assistant types are easier to find and keep separate.

ai.title: Add self-validation step to gpt-5-worker prompt
ai.summary: Updated the `base2-gpt-5-worker` agent prompt in `.agents/base2/base2-gpt-5-worker.ts` to include an explicit step for running validation commands (typechecks, tests, lints) before completion. This change ensures the worker agent actively verifies its own edits rather than relying solely on the parent agent for review. The scope is limited to the internal agent definition file.

eli5.text: When our code-assistant agent finishes writing new code, it now has an extra step built into its instructions: it must run the project's checks on itself (like type checks, tests, and linters) before reporting back to its supervising system. Previously the assistant would just make the edits and ask the supervisor to double-check; now the assistant actively verifies its own work first. This affects the internal automated agents that write code for us, and you'd notice it in the form of fewer mistakes needing correction after the fact.

ai.title: Add runId to agent runtime and SDK contracts
ai.summary: Propagate `runId` through `PromptAiSdkFn`, `PromptAiSdkStreamFn`, and `runAgentStep` in `common/src/types/contracts/llm.ts` and `packages/agent-runtime`. This links LLM calls and tool executions to specific agent runs for better tracing. Updates affect CLI hooks, evals scaffolding, and SDK dependencies.

eli5.text: Each time you ask the assistant to do something, that request is now tagged with a unique run ID that follows the request through the entire process. This lets the system trace which large language model calls and tool actions belong to your specific request, making it easier to debug or analyze what happened during a run. The run ID is passed through the core contracts used by CLI hooks, evaluation scaffolding, and the agent runtime, including the live-user-inputs and send-message paths. If you looked at the internals, you'd see new runId fields added to the types used by SDK calls and agent steps, plus new dependency wiring like the agent-runtime being added to the SDK package. The feature is live today on 2025-10-23 and affects CLI users, the evaluation harness, and the agent runtime

ai.title: Fix malformed-tool-call test mock
ai.summary: Added requestFiles mock to processStreamWithTools in malformed-tool-call.test.ts. Prevents test failures by providing file content during stream processing. Scope limited to agent-runtime test suite. Mock returns `${path} content` for each filePath.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team fixed a test that checks how the agent handles broken tool calls. They added a small stand-in that supplies file contents during that test so it runs smoothly. You wouldn't notice this at all - it only affects internal testing of the agent system and doesn't change anything you see or use.

ai.title: Add Buffy orchestrator and file researcher agents
ai.summary: New internal agents added under .agents/base2 and .agents/researcher. base2-with-file-researcher.ts defines 'Buffy the Orchestrator' using base2/fast, spawning file-researcher and context-pruner. file-researcher.ts implements a Sonnet 4.5 agent that generates structured reports and file lists via specialized sub-agents like file-picker-max and code-searcher.

eli5.text: The developer tools now include two new helper assistants that work behind the scenes on coding tasks. One helper (Buffy) coordinates the work by sending out specialized sub-helpers, including another helper (File Researcher) that quickly scans code and produces a short written summary of the relevant parts plus a list of files. These run automatically when developers use the orchestrator path, which was added today as a new internal workflow. Nothing about the product itself changes; this only affects how the internal development assistants search and report on code.

ai.title: Deprecate checkConnection
ai.summary: CodebuffClient.checkConnection in sdk/src/client.ts is deprecated. Implementation replaced with static true return, removing WebSocket dependency and timeout logic. Scope limited to SDK client. Method remains callable for backward compatibility.

eli5.text: The SDK used to open a network connection to the assistant service every time it checked whether the service was online, then closed it a few seconds later if nothing happened. That check now just hands back a 'yes' right away without making any network call, so the old way of testing connectivity no longer actually tests anything. If you are calling that check from your own code, it will still run but only returns true regardless of whether the service is really reachable today. Because the method is still callable, existing programs keep working, but the connection-probing behavior that used to back it is gone.

ai.title: Export getUserInfoFromApiKey from SDK
ai.summary: SDK now exports `getUserInfoFromApiKey`. `OpenRouterProviderOptions` type moved from internal package to `common/src/types/agent-template.ts`. `common/src/types/contracts/database.ts` imports updated to use absolute paths.

eli5.text: If you're an app developer using this toolkit to build tools that work with us, you can now pull account information directly from an API string without needing to keep the lookup logic inside your own code. The function that does this has been exposed as part of the toolkit's public package, alongside a cleanup that moves one of its helper definitions to a shared location so it can be reused reliably. For the same change to take effect on your end, you'll want to update your imported package version; otherwise you'll just get an 'unresolved' error when you try to import it.

ai.title: Remove runId parameter from startAgentRun
ai.summary: Removed optional runId parameter from startAgentRun in backend/src/agent-run.ts. Function now always generates new UUID via crypto.randomUUID(). Prevents duplicate runIds when caller passes existing ID.

eli5.text: Each time the assistant begins a new task, the system now always assigns it a fresh, unique tracking number instead of letting callers try to supply their own or reuse an old one. This prevents two different task runs from accidentally sharing the same tracking number, which could cause confusion in records. You won't see this directly, but it keeps task logging cleaner behind the scenes.

ai.title: fix $$ in str replace
ai.summary: Updated processStrReplace in packages/agent-runtime/src/process-str-replace.ts to pass a function to String.prototype.replaceAll instead of a string. This prevents special replacement patterns like $$ from being interpreted in the replacement string. Scope limited to Agent Runtime string replacement logic.

eli5.text: The assistant now handles text replacements correctly when your content includes a dollar sign followed by another dollar sign. Previously, typing $$ in your instructions or files could cause the replacement to behave unexpectedly because the program treated $$ as a special code. The fix makes replacements treat your text literally, so what you write is exactly what gets inserted. If you ever tried to include $$ in a file or instruction and it came out wrong, that should no longer happen.

ai.title: Remove runId parameter from startAgentRun
ai.summary: Removed optional `runId` parameter from `StartAgentRunFn` type and `startAgentRun` implementation. Function now generates `runId` internally via `crypto.randomUUID()` instead of accepting it as input. Affects `backend/src/agent-run.ts`, `common/src/types/contracts/database.ts`, and `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`. Callers no longer pass `runId` to `startAgentRun`.

eli5.text: When a new agent run starts, the system now creates its own unique ID internally instead of requiring callers to pass one in. This removes a now-redundant step from the agent startup process and slightly shrinks the configuration needed to kick off a run. If you were wiring up agent runs, you no longer pass a run ID; the system generates it for you.

ai.title: Fix backend test expectation for agent run ID
ai.summary: Updated `agent-run.test.ts` to expect `runId: 'generated-uuid'` instead of `undefined` in logger error assertions. This aligns the test with actual backend behavior where run IDs are generated even during error states. Scope limited to `backend/src/__tests__/agent-run.test.ts`.

eli5.text: The system's behind-the-scenes checks that make sure everything works correctly have been quietly updated to match how the system actually behaves now. If you were looking at the testing tools, you'd notice that one of the test scenarios now expects the system to correctly track which task it's working on, even when something goes wrong. This is live today as a subtle improvement to how the system monitors itself, and it mainly affects the developers who maintain the software rather than everyday users.
